subject: AI & Agents
title: The Knowledge Cutoff Problem
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Knowledge Cutoff Problem.

hook.text: Ask an LLM about yesterday's news and it has no idea. Its world stopped at the training cutoff.

buildup.text: LLMs are frozen in time — they only know what existed in their training data.

discovery.text: A model trained in 2023 doesn't know about events in 2024, no matter how important.

twist.text: Web search plugins and RAG help, but the base model itself remains stuck in the past.

climax.text: Users often don't realize they're talking to a snapshot, not a live oracle.

punchline.text: AI knows the past deeply and the present not at all.

quiz.question: What is the knowledge cutoff problem?
options: LLMs only know information from before their training ended
LLMs can only answer one question per session

details.summary: LLMs only know information from their training data, which has a cutoff date. They cannot access current events, recent discoveries, or updated facts unless given external tools or retrieval systems.
details.whyItMatters: Users often expect AI to know everything, including yesterday's news. The knowledge cutoff explains outdated answers and drives solutions like RAG and web search integration.
takeaways: LLM knowledge ends at the training data cutoff date
Events after the cutoff are unknown unless provided externally
RAG and web search tools extend LLM knowledge to current data

faq.question: When is the knowledge cutoff for major models?
faq.answer: It varies by model and version. GPT-4's cutoff is typically months before release. Models are continuously updated but always have some lag. The cutoff date is usually disclosed in model documentation.

faq.question: How can the knowledge cutoff be addressed?
faq.answer: RAG retrieval adds current information to prompts. Web search plugins fetch real-time data. Fine-tuning on recent data can update knowledge but is expensive. The most practical solution is combining the LLM with external tools.
